After recovery heat treatment, each precipitated phase and aberrant structure of the alloy dissolved into the austenite matrix, generating a supersaturated solid solution, then precipitated a ﬁne and uniform intracrystalline b phase and a tiny bar grain boundary b phase (Fig. 5d and e).
Then, the coarse b phase formed the chain structure, which destroyed the continuity and uniformity of the alloy microstructure (Fig. 5a, b, and c).
At the same time, twins formed, and grain boundaries got wider, which made the alloy work better at high temperatures.
The fracture mode evolved from ductile to brittle with time, indicating that grain boundary strength and plasticity were decreasing
The microhardness of the b phase was observed to decrease from 307 to 284 HV and 274 HV as service time increased.
The yield strength of the material increased from 810 to 884 MPa, an increase of 9.1%, as predicted by the change rule in Eq 2.
